entries.title: Man, 18, shot multiple times in Little Village
entries.summary:
An 18-year-old man was in serious condition after a shooting Saturday afternoon in Little Village, Chicago police said.

The man was walking near the sidewalk in the 3300 block of West 31st Street about 3:16 p.m. when a vehicle approached and at least one person inside fired multiple shots at him, police said.

The man was taken to Mount Sinai Hospital in serious condition.

Area Four detectives are investigating.

entries.title: Chicago Archdiocese clears retired priest accused of sexual abuse, approves return to ministry
entries.summary: <p>The Archdiocese of Chicago is allowing a retired priest to return to ministry after the church's independent review board found no reasonable cause to believe he had abused a minor decades ago.</p><p>In a letter distributed Saturday to six parish communities, Cardinal Blase Cupich said he had accepted the review board’s recommendation to close the case against the Rev. Kenneth Fleck.</p><p>The archdiocese received the allegation in July, more than 30 years after the alleged abuse occurred. Fleck served as pastor of Our Lady of Peace from May 1984 to August 1996, during which the abuse was alleged to have occurred.</p><p>Three months ago, Cupich asked the priest to step away from ministry while civil authorities and the archdiocese’s Independent Review Board investigated the allegation. The archdiocese also said it had been informed a lawsuit alleging sexual abuse of a minor would be filed.</p><p>Fleck strongly denied the allegation and cooperated with the investigation, according to Cupich’s letter. He said Fleck is a priest in good standing and expressed appreciation for his years of service to the archdiocese.</p><p>"It is important to stress that the welfare of the children entrusted to our care is of paramount importance," Cupich wrote. "For this reason, we take all allegations of sexual misconduct seriously. At the same time, we must restore the good name of anyone so accused when the allegations are found to be unsubstantiated."</p><p>Fleck also served at St. Barnabas, St. Josephine Bakhita and St. Katherine Drexel, all in Chicago, as well as St. Catherine of Alexandria in Oak Lawn, Christ Our Savior in South Holland and St. George in Tinley Park.</p><p>The archdiocese also encouraged anyone who has experienced sexual abuse by a priest, deacon, religious or lay employee to come forward.</p>

entries.title: Bulls' Noa Essengue was back on the bench but out of the doghouse
entries.summary: <p>It’s tough for coach <b>Tiago Splitter</b> to guess how many minutes <b>Noa Essengue</b> was going to get on Saturday against the Wizards.</p><p>The second-year forward has emerged in that rotation mix of the No. 9 or No. 10 guy, based on matchup, according to Splitter, and he insisted that he planned to lean more on <b>Zach Collins</b>, anyway, because of his physicality in the paint counters what the Wizards bring to the floor.</p><p>By tip-off Essengue’s minutes weren’t an issue, however, with the medical staff deciding that the light sensitivity Essengue was experiencing after he took a shot in the head during Friday’s victory against the Bucks was enough to sideline him for a night.</p><p>Not exactly great timing since Essengue had by far his most productive minutes of his career against the Bucks, but again a reminder that the 19-year-old is still a project.</p><p>At least he’s one that Splitter and the organization feel a little better about.</p><p>Not the case in July, when Essengue’s effort and his habit of being overly emotional didn’t sit well with Splitter. What ended up sitting well with the coach was Essengue, benched throughout Summer League.</p><p>Message received.</p><p>“It was a strong message,” Essengue told the Sun-Times last week. “To see my playing time cut in Summer League because they said I don’t put any force or energy on the court, it was something where it just forces you to change it, to put that force out there.”</p><p>That mentality earned Essengue 10 minutes of work in the blowout to the Raptors, but saw that bump to 17 minutes against the Bucks. And his role is simple: Be a disrupter on defense with his length.</p><p>Splitter did reiterate that Essengue’s presence on the floor was match-up based from game-to-game, but at least the forward is seemingly out of Splitter’s doghouse.</p><p>“There’s a feel of course,” Splitter explained on Saturday when asked about handling Essengue with tough love. “From the first meeting I had with him, he asked me to be coached hard, that’s what I did. I told him the truth, I was honest with him, and he reacted.</p><p>“Kudos to him to approach it differently. Yes, he can make mistakes but at least he’s trying to do the right thing and he’s playing hard. That’s my take on him.”</p><p><b>Odd man out</b></p><p>It continues to be very clear that <b>Patrick Williams</b> has not only fallen out of the rotation but is not even a thought come mop-up time. He was the only active player to not get minutes in the blowout loss to Toronto on Wednesday and didn’t sniff the court in the Bucks win.</p><p>That wasn’t an issue Saturday, however, with Williams being ruled out with a sore groin. It was not believed to be serious.</p><p><b>For openers</b></p><p>Even going back to the preseason, the Bulls’ starting unit hasn’t looked connected for extended period of times. Maybe it’s the group still trying to figure out Splitter’s system and executing it more consistently or maybe it’s just growing pains because of all the changes.</p><p>Rookie <b>Caleb Wilson</b> didn’t sound overly concerned with the starting group.</p><p>“Sometimes it does [look stagnant] but that’s just basketball,” Wilson said of the slow starts. “We’re all playing together, we have a new coach, a new system, some of us are new to the team, and I’m one of the focal points of the team and I’m a rookie in the NBA trying to figure it out myself.</p><p>“It’s stuff we have to work on and get the chemistry on, get better and better.”</p>

entries.title: Bulls fall to the Wizards as tough love lessons continue being learned
entries.summary: <p>The principles that coach Tiago Splitter has preached are easy to grasp: Play hard and you’ll play late.</p><p>Salary amount and contract length don’t matter. Experience alone need not apply. It is a simple ideology and one that the Bulls coach deems non-negotiable.</p><p>That was evident in Friday’s win in Milwaukee as crunch time came and the likes of Josh Giddey and Matas Buzelis were nowhere to be found. A night later in the home opener against the Wizards at the United Center, Giddey and Buzelis had a bit more urgency off the tip, letting their coach know that the message had been heard loud and clear.</p><p>Now the next lesson needs to be about staying power for 48 minutes, as the Bulls (1-2) overcame a disastrous third quarter in which they were doubled up 40-20, to make it a game late before falling 124-120.</p><p>And yes, Giddey and Buzelis were on the floor for closing time.</p><p>“We were very inconsistent with our coverages,” Splitter said of the third-quarter issues. “We didn’t take the best shots that third quarter. We’ve got to be smarter. It was really tough for us to score. For us to win basketball games we’ve got to play 48 minutes.”</p><p>Buzelis was more harsh with his assessment of the third, pointing the finger at himself.</p><p>“We gotta be ready to play,” Buzelis said. “Part of that is on me, being a leader on this team. We should have easily won that game.”</p><p>Call it baby steps.</p><p>The one player who is a baby in NBA years but continues to play anything like a 20-year-old rookie? Caleb Wilson not only finished with 30 points and 14 rebounds but also put on an aerial assault of the rim not seen by a Bulls player in quite a few years.</p><p>If the NBA Rookie of the Year campaign was waiting for a first-year player to move the needle, Wilson did more than jump-start it on Saturday with five first-half dunks.</p><p>“Just being aggressive,” Wilson said of his mentality to attack the paint. “The Wizards are really big, and our opportunities are in transition because they have so much size.”</p><p>With 30 points, 14 rebounds and two steals, Wilson became the third-youngest player in NBA history to put up those minimums, joining John Drew and Victor Wembanyama.</p><p>But the big picture through the first few games for the Bulls is the mentality that Splitter is trying to instill and the penalty for the players who don’t get it.</p><p>“In general players got to compete every possession and we’re not there yet,” Splitter said. “But that’s how I believe they get better. They need pressure. They need to have minutes as well, but they need to feel the pressure of when they’re not playing the way I want, you’re going to sit with me for a little bit.”</p><p>Buzelis actually sat with Splitter a lot in Milwaukee, like the entire fourth quarter. The two spoke before the Wizards game and that’s why the coach tried to downplay how big of a deal it was.</p><p>“We’re making it a bigger deal than it should be,” Splitter said.</p><p>Buzelis showed a bounce back, scoring 10 points in the first half against the Wizards and finishing with 21. And tough love for Buzelis was nothing new, considering that’s how former coach Billy Donovan handled the young forward in their time together.</p><p>Still, Year 3 for Buzelis was supposed to be different. Splitter wants to make sure it will be: “He’s a 22-year-old, he’s still learning.”</p>

entries.title: The Fire knock off Atlanta United to earn second consecutive 50-point season
entries.summary: <p>ATLANTA — Anton Salétros had a goal and an assist to help the Chicago Fire rally for a 3-2 victory over Atlanta United on Saturday night.</p><p>With the victory, Chicago (15-10-6) reached the 50-point plateau in back-to-back seasons for the second time in club history — also doing so in 2000-01.</p><p>Atlanta United took a 1-0 lead in the 4th minute when first-year defender Tomás Jacob took passes from Miguel Almirón and Mauricio Amaro and scored his fourth goal. Almirón's assist was his eighth of the season and Amaro collected his first in his ninth career appearance.</p><p>Chicago pulled even on the second goal by Salétros, unassisted in the 30th minute and the tie stood through halftime.</p><p>The Fire took a 2-1 lead in the 51st minute when Anzor Mekvabishvili stole the ball and scored his first goal in his third appearance in the league.</p><p>Chicago grabbed a two-goal lead in the 60th minute when Salétros notched his third assist in setting up Philip Zinckernagel for his sixth netter this season.</p><p>Breel Embolo used his head to score off a long assist from Elías Báez to cut it to 3-2 eight minutes later. Amaro was also credited with an assist on Embolo's second goal in his first nine MLS matches.</p><p>Chris Brady finished with one save for Chicago, which snapped a two-match skid.</p><p>Lucas Hoyos did not have a save for Atlanta United (8-17-6). The club's 10 losses at home this season are the most in the league.</p><p>The Fire beat Atlanta United 1-0 at Soldier Field in early April.</p><p><b>Up next</b></p><p>Chicago: Hosts Orlando City on Wednesday.</p><p>Atlanta: At New York City FC on Wednesday.</p>

entries.title: Dear Abby: Neighbor's unruly granddaughter skates on thin ice
entries.summary: <p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> My next-door neighbor, "Dee," has a granddaughter, "Sarah." A year ago, I was friendly with Sarah, but months later, she became disrespectful. She wouldn't listen when I asked her not to ring my doorbell for no reason or tease my cats. I told Dee, and she said she would try to talk to her. Dee said she can't make Sarah mind at times.</p><p>The misbehavior stopped briefly until about two weeks ago. Now Sarah skates back and forth in front of my apartment. I didn't think much about it until I caught her watching me when I'm outside. What do you do when you want to stay friends with a neighbor but she has a teen that won't stop acting up? I need some ideas. — <i>ANNOYED IN KENTUCKY</i></p><p><b>DEAR ANNOYED:</b> Stay friends with Dee by continuing to treat her as a friend — as long as Sarah behaves herself. Saying she "can't make Sarah mind" is no excuse. As the adult in the household, Dee is responsible for anything Sarah does, and you should react accordingly.</p><p>I don't think "watching you" is an offense worth risking your friendship with Dee over, but if Sarah's antics escalate to their previous levels, inform Dee and tell her you expect her to control her granddaughter. If Sarah ever resorts to outright criminal behavior, call the police immediately.</p><p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> My mother-in-law moved in with my husband and me seven months ago. It has been difficult from the beginning. We got along pretty well before she came to live with us. It happened pretty quickly, and we really didn't get to discuss it.</p><p>She doesn't offer to help with the cooking or cleaning. Of course, costs went up — electricity, groceries and the water bill. We pay for everything. We take her to her doctors, but she doesn't do what they recommend. We even pay for her prescriptions with no offer from her to reimburse us. She is disrespectful toward me, and I don't like being around her.</p><p>My husband does everything for her. He helped her with her bills, packing up her house and putting everything in storage. I understand she is his mom, but she never acted like a mother. She has never sent birthday cards or acknowledged our children or grandchildren. She was and is all about herself.</p><p>My husband asks me, "What am I supposed to do, kick her out?" I feel this has gone on long enough and we three need to sit down and talk, which we should have done a long time ago. How can we sort this out? — <i>HEAVY-HEARTED IN MISSOURI</i></p><p><b>DEAR HEAVY-HEARTED:</b> You and your husband should have had a frank discussion about this before his mother was invited to move in. Because that didn't happen then, do it now. By all means, call for a meeting of the three of you because it is overdue. Before the meeting, make a list of the things you feel your MIL should be helping with so you can refer to it. That her things are all in storage may be a blessing, in case she needs to relocate again.</p><p>Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren. For nearly four decades, Jeanne Phillips penned this column, which was founded in 1956 by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 270135, Kansas City, MO 64127. </p>

entries.title: Bears' defense looks great one moment, shaky the next, so what exactly is this group?
entries.summary: <p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a>’ defense has been all over the place this season, and it was as erratic as ever <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/22/bears-inactives-vs-patriots-lb-t-j-edwards-out-with-hamstring-injury" target="_blank" >in their 30-24 victory Thursday against the Patriots</a> at Soldier Field.</p><p>The defense opened by forcing a turnover on downs and two three-and-outs, then got an interception in the end zone by linebacker D’Marco Jackson to keep points off the board. It also was fantastic on third downs, holding the Patriots to 2-for-7.</p><p>But it allowed an exasperating, inexcusable 48-yard touchdown pass just before halftime on a throw underneath from quarterback Drake Maye to running back Rhamondre Stevenson.</p><p>The Bears shut down the Patriots’ running game but got torched by Maye for one of the best games of his career.</p><p>Kyler Gordon suddenly looks as though he’s going to make a run at Defensive Player of the Year, but Jaylon Johnson has struggled for weeks.</p><p>So what exactly is this defense? Even coach Ben Johnson had a tough time pinpointing that Friday as he sized up a unit that has allowed the most yards per play in the NFL (6.3) but ranks eighth in points allowed (20.4).</p><p>‘‘I hate to look back at last year, but we’re a better defense than we were a year ago,’’ he said. ‘‘[But] we’re not taking the ball away quite as much. If we can continue to harp on getting those takeaways, you’re going to see more consistent defensive play.’’</p><p>The Bears led the NFL with 33 takeaways last season; they’re on pace for 24 this season.</p><p>Johnson saw what he wanted in the defense’s ‘‘super-hot’’ start, but Maye started punching back in the second quarter and never stopped. He finished 24-for-31 for 321 yards with two touchdowns and an interception for a 117.8 passer rating.</p><p>While Johnson gives defensive coordinator Dennis Allen autonomy, he’s highly engaged in that side of the ball, even as the offensive play-caller. Whereas Matt Eberflus sounded lost when talking about offense and Matt Nagy struggled to discuss defense, Johnson has a clear vision of how he wants the Bears to play defensively.</p><p>‘‘Our play style is the most important thing,’’ he said, pointing to an aggressive, physical approach in which swarms of tacklers converge on the ball.</p><p>He called that last part ‘‘non-negotiable’’ and was dismayed by how badly the Bears failed in it on Stevenson’s big play. They faltered at every level of the defense, and Johnson vented that his staff had spent ample time practicing for situations just like that.</p><p>The Bears lined up in a prevent coverage with two safeties at the goal line, and there were five defenders between Stevenson and the end zone when he caught the ball at the Bears’ 46. Yet he barely was touched.</p><p>That play changed the game.</p><p>If the Bears had been able to close out the final 14 seconds of the first half, they would have come out of halftime with a 20-7 lead and the ball. They could have buried the Patriots at that point. Instead, the game went down to the final minutes, and they needed a career-long 58-yard field goal from Cairo Santos to ensure victory.</p><p>The week before, the Bears let a 31-7 lead in the fourth quarter dwindle to a one-score game in which the Falcons had the ball and a chance to tie the game with more than three minutes left.</p><p>The Bears know better than anyone not to play around like that. Their run of comebacks last season had as much to do with opposing defenses whiffing on chances to finish them off as it did with the offensive heroics of Caleb Williams and others, and they’re now leaving that door open for their opponents.</p><p>Six of their remaining 10 games are against teams in the top half of the NFL in scoring, so they’re unlikely to continue getting away with such inconsistency.</p>

entries.title: Bears QB Caleb Williams fined $11,941 for wearing Tom Brady-backed Caddix cleats; Another fine likely coming
entries.summary: <p>The NFL fined <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> quarterback <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2024/08/30/caleb-williams-wins-bears-over-with-rare-talent-but-even-rarer-people-skills" >Caleb Williams</a> $11,941 for the cleats he wore against the Falcons in his return from a hamstring injury, and he’ll likely be paying another fine for wearing them again Thursday in the win over the Patriots.</p><p>The league said it fined Williams for a uniform violation because he wore cleats made by Caddix, a relatively new company that says the studs it uses will reduce non-contact knee and ankle injuries.</p><p>The NFL has partnerships with only Nike, adidas and Under Armour, so if a player wears a shoe made by any other brand, he must cover the logo. Players can’t promote any non-partner on game days, from pre-game warmups through post-game media availability, and the league noted its letter to Williams that the policy was communicated to all players before the season.</p><p>Williams appeared to wear Caddix cleats in the first two games of the season, including when he suffered a hamstring injury against the Vikings, but they were all white, so the logo wasn’t prominent enough to cause an issue. In the Falcons and Patriots games, Williams wore black cleats with the gray Caddix logo clearly visible.</p><p>He was tremendous in both games. He completed 75.4% of his passes, totaled 613 yards and threw three touchdown passes with no turnovers for a 116.4 passer rating. The victory over the Patriots pushed the Bears to 5-2 heading into an extended break leading up to their Nov. 2 game at the defending champion Seahawks.</p><p>Williams has not had a shoe contract since entering the NFL as the No. 1 overall pick in 2024, which is unusual. Most players of his status have one, but he hasn’t wanted to be boxed in and has frequently worn Nike and New Balance. He wore Nike cleats in his debut and frequently since.</p><p>Hall of Famer Tom Brady works with Caddix and wore their cleats in the Fanatics flag football event this year. Williams has been friends with Brady since reaching the NFL, and Brady occasionally is on the Fox broadcast team for Bears games.</p><p>Bengals quarterback Joe Flacco and 49ers fullback Kyle Juszczyk also have worn the cleats, and the company said roughly 40 players are wearing them this season.</p><p>Caddix, based in Baltimore, produced its first cleats in 2024 and has made inroads in football, soccer and lacrosse. The brand has jumped on the opportunity for publicity with Williams wearing the cleats, and CEO Jack Rasmussen said in a statement the company will pay any fines he receives.</p><p>The NFL fines players $5,971 for uniform violations of having a foreign substance on their uniform, using noncompliant pads and facemasks, an unapproved visor and wearing the uniform improperly. The $11,941 fine applies to displaying personal messages or unauthorized logos.</p><p>Williams has until Oct. 30 to appeal the fine for the Falcons game.</p><p>The NFL also fined Bears wide receiver Jahdae Walker $5,620 for each of his penalties in the Falcons game. Walker was flagged for hitting Falcons punter Jake Bailey in the third quarter and ejected for headbutting wide receiver Chris Blair after a play in the fourth.</p>

entries.title: 1 killed, 2 injured in shooting at West Garfield Park gas station
entries.summary: <p>Three men were shot, one fatally, at a West Garfield Park gas station late Saturday night, Chicago police said.</p><p>The men were at the gas station in the 400 block of South Kostner Avenue around 10 p.m. when a white SUV pulled up and three armed men got out and started firing shots at them, according to police. The gunmen then returned to the car and fled the scene. </p><p>One of the men, 30 years old, was shot in the neck and pronounced dead at Mount Sinai Hospital, police said. The other two, both 28, were also shot: one was in critical condition at Mount Sinai and the other was shot in the knee and taken in good condition to Stroger Hospital.</p><p>Police have not announced any arrests. </p>

entries.title: Lake Street bridge closure for CTA Green, Pink lines extended 2 days
entries.summary: <p>CTA Green and Pink line trains will continue to be rerouted this week as ongoing construction on the Lake Street bridge is behind schedule by two days. </p><p>The two train lines were <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/transportation/2026/10/12/lake-street-bridge-cta-green-pink" target="_blank" >rerouted two weeks ago</a> to accommodate the ongoing repairs to the Lake Street bridge over the Chicago River. Those repairs are behind, the Chicago Department of Transportation announced Sunday. </p><p>Green and Pink line trains were set to resume their normal routes on Monday, but CDOT says that won't happen till Wednesday at 4 a.m. </p><p>Pink Line trains are currently not running through the Loop. Instead, the train line terminates at Racine, where riders can transfer to the Blue Line.</p><p>The Green Line has been operating in two separate sections. The Lake Street branch ends at Clinton, where riders can take a free shuttle bus to the Clark/Lake station. The Green Line’s southern branch continues running to the Loop, but winds around stations in a clockwise direction before returning south again.</p><p>The bridge has been closed to pedestrians and vehicle traffic for <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago/2025/09/28/lake-street-bridge-repairs-closure-chicago" target="_blank" >just over a year</a> for renovation. Construction is estimated to last until January 2028.</p>

entries.title: Optimist vs. Pessimist: There's no limit to what the Bears can do over the final 10 games
entries.summary: <p><i>For Patrick Finley's pessimistic look at the Bears' next 10 games, </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/authors/patrick-finley" target="_blank" ><i>click here</i></a><i>.</i></p><p>The current version of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >the Bears</a> requires some rewiring of the brain for anyone who has watched this team the last four decades. It’s the same uniform, the same logo and the same field, but a very different operation.</p><p>It’s no longer inevitable, or even probable, that the Bears will fall apart. The annual tradition of a four-to-six-game losing streak is done. There’s competency across the board, as evidenced by their impressive win over the Patriots, managing well during quarterback Caleb Williams’ three-game absence and the fact that they’ve won 17 of their last 24 games.</p><p>There’s every reason to be optimistic about where the Bears are headed, and it starts with coach Ben Johnson.</p><p>The mentality of the entire organization changed when he arrived. Goals got greater, standards got stricter and doubt got demolished. There had been a feeling of resignation toward certain realities, like the Packers’ dominance, but it’s not there anymore.</p><p>At 5-2, the Bears are in position to chase everything they want this season.</p><p>The schedule certainly gets tougher, but none of their remaining 10 games are daunting enough to concede. Even in the Nov. 2 visit to the defending champion Seahawks, the early line has the Bears as a negligible three-point underdog.</p><p>At their best, they have every piece necessary to make a run at the Super Bowl: a savvy head coach who has a handle on both sides of the ball, a game-changing quarterback surrounded by weapons and a dynamic defense.</p><p>Are they flawed? Yes, but that’s true of every team. It comes down to how well they can scheme around their flaws and compensate for them. Johnson and defensive coordinator Dennis Allen have consistently shown that ability.</p><p>The starting point on discussing whether any team can win a title is the coach and quarterback. For the first time in recent memory, the Bears check those boxes.</p><p>Johnson’s credibility is high enough that he pretty much skated on a botched trick play Thursday in which Williams handed the ball off illegally to left guard Joe Thuney. He brushed it off with, “Shooters shoot,” and it’s hard to imagine any recent Bears coach getting away with that.</p><p>He has shown an uncommon ability to adjust, whereas previous Bears teams had no shot if Plan A crumbled. He’s fully engaged in the defense and special teams, even though they aren’t his areas of expertise. And, most of all, he’s developing Williams into a championship-caliber quarterback.</p><p>The high-end talent was obvious with Williams his first two seasons, but he lacked a foundation. Johnson has helped establish the essentials — throwing accuracy, coverage recognition, quick reads, precise timing — and blended that with his remarkable improvisational skills.</p><p>If that continues, the Bears will finish at least 12-5. They won’t necessarily sweep their road games against the Seahawks, Bills and Lions — a tough ask for anyone — but, at minimum, they’ll hold their own.</p><p>This is a team that nearly made the NFC Championship Game last season and is playing better this season. There’s no limit on who the Bears can play with and how far they can go.</p>

entries.title: Bulls slowly figuring some things out but schedule about to turn brutal
entries.summary: <p>As the upcoming schedule was being recited to Caleb Wilson, the rookie really didn’t need the reminder.</p><p>“It’s rough …” he said before hearing a second meeting with Boston later in the week.</p><p>“Rough” is one way to look at it for the Bulls. Gauntlet, daunting, brutal also all come to mind, starting Monday with the first of two against the Celtics this week.</p><p>Throw in two with the defending NBA Champions in the Knicks, two against the new-look 76ers, and then a home game on Nov. 11 against Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs?</p><p>Wilson and the Bulls are about to be tested.</p><p>“Every matchup is its own thing,” Wilson said. “Not every team has a Wemby, not every team has a Jayson Tatum, so every game we go out there with the approach that we need to be great players and do what we need to do because it’s about us.</p><p>“I feel like with this team we’re really well-rounded, and I feel like that’s going to be to our benefit. I like us so I’m excited for the opportunity.”</p><p>The silver lining coming out of the weekend for the Bulls? The starting group finally seemed to grasp some cohesion. Enough so that coach Tiago Splitter believed enough in the group to try and finish the game against the Wizards with them.</p><p>That wasn’t the case Friday afternoon in Milwaukee when Splitter benched the likes of Matas Buzelis and Josh Giddey for the hot hands of Isaac Okoro and Tre Jones. Yet, against the Wizards in that final stanza it was Giddey’s play-making, evident by his six assists and plus-10 in plus/minus in the fourth, and Buzelis, who chipped in with nine points, that contributed to the attempted comeback.</p><p>Contributed, but not lead it.</p><p>No, that was the 20-year-old rookie in Wilson who scored 11 of his 30 points, grabbed five rebounds and handed out two assists. The second-straight game in which Wilson was the focal point in crunch time.</p><p>“I feel like it shows that we have fight, but we put ourselves in that position,” Wilson said of the late-game push against Washington. “I wouldn’t say I’d give us a moral victory but it’s good to know the character of the guys we have on this team.”</p><p>Character that is about to be tested by arguably the toughest stretch the Bulls (1-2) will likely have this season.</p><p>Wilson understands that but is also trying to embrace it.</p><p>If the starting unit can continue to build the connectivity they showed against Washington that will go a long way in trying to navigate the next seven games.</p><p>“Just an unselfishness, being able to move the ball, being able to trust each other,” Wilson said about the starting unit growing. “That’s all that really happened and it led to a really good start, but you got to do it for 48 minutes.”</p><p>One positive in facing Boston, New York and Philadelphia? None of their starting units goes with a double-big lineup. Washington had Anthony Davis and Alex Sarr starting at the same time, staggering in Deandre Ayton.</p><p>The Celtics start Mitchell Robinson in the middle but it’s more about the versatile wings in Paul George and Tatum. The Knicks have length up front with Karl-Anthony Towns, OG Anunoby and Mikal Bridges, but again, not two true bigs.</p><p>“I’m really tall but I’m on the thinner side, so I just try and run and be faster than everyone, but honestly I feel like the biggest adjustment in playing double bigs is knowing you have to box out and be physical,” Wilson said. “That was one of my biggest things (against the Wizards).”</p><p>Double bigs or no bigs, Wilson is going to have to be physical either way over the next few weeks with what’s coming.</p><p>“Like I said,” he added. “It’s going to be rough.”</p>

entries.title: 1 killed, 2 injured in shooting at West Garfield Park gas station
entries.summary: <p>Three men were shot, one fatally, at a West Garfield Park gas station late Saturday night, Chicago police said.</p><p>The men were at the gas station in the 400 block of South Kostner Avenue around 10 p.m. when a white SUV pulled up and three armed men got out and started firing shots at them, according to police. The gunmen then returned to the car and fled the scene. </p><p>One of the men, 30 years old, was shot in the neck and pronounced dead at Mount Sinai Hospital, police said. The other two, both 28, were also shot: one was in critical condition at Mount Sinai and the other was shot in the knee and taken in good condition to Stroger Hospital.</p><p>Police have not announced any arrests. </p>

entries.title: Optimist vs. Pessimist: Bears could struggle to dig out of NFC North hole
entries.summary: <p><i>For Jason Lieser's optimistic look at the Bears' next 10 games, click </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/25/optimist-vs-pessimist-theres-no-limit-on-what-the-bears-can-do-over-the-final-10-games" target="_blank" ><i>here</i></a><i>.</i></p><p>It’s easy to be optimistic about the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a>’ first seven games. It gets harder to do so when you look at their final 10.</p><p>For all their success this season — to be 5-2 after starting three different quarterbacks is nothing short of remarkable — the Bears have struggled where it matters most: against the rest of the NFC North. Both their losses have come to divisional opponents: the Vikings in Week 2 and the Packers in an embarrassing Week 5.</p><p>The Bears have four more divisional games to play, starting with a Thanksgiving game against the Lions at Ford Field. To take the NFC North for the second-straight season, they’ll probably need to run the table against the Packers, Vikings and Lions.</p><p>That’s a difficult hill to climb, one far tougher than anything they’ve accomplished to this point this season. But if the Bears have their eyes on the NFC championship — and they should, given the way they’ve played — they know they have to position themselves to play as many playoff games at home as possible.<br>The Bears proved last year what a tremendous impact both their home crowd and freezing temperatures — wind chill was 26 degrees in the first playoff game and 11 in the second — can have in January.</p><p>They can’t put themselves in the same position this year without winning the NFC North. And they can’t win the NFC North without winning head-to-head matchups. At the least, they can’t count on it happening again.</p><p>When the Bears won the NFC North last year, they did so with just a 2-4 record. That had happened only two other times in the modern history of the sport, provided you throw out the 1982 strike year. Since the AFL-NFL merger in 1970, just two other teams won their division despite going 2-4 within it: the 1971 49ers and the 2010 Chiefs.</p><p>Bears coach Ben Johnson has never beaten the Lions. That needs to change for the Bears to get where they want to go. A Christmas Day matchup against the Packers looms large, too — if the Packers, win they’ll hold the tie-breaker against their rivals. And then there are the Vikings, the team that leads the NFC North. At the start of the year, the Bears could look at their season finale in Minneapolis and dream of a scenario in which the Vikings, eliminated from the playoffs and perhaps chasing a better draft pick, simply rolled over. A lot would have to go wrong for the Vikings, who had the best defense in the NFL entering Sunday’s games, to freefall into irrelevance by Week 18.</p><p>The Bears’ schedule the rest of the season features two of the best three teams in the AFC: the Jaguars at home and the Bills on the road. The defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks await the Bears next week in Seattle, where they’ve lost just one game the past two seasons to teams not named the 49ers.</p><p>But nothing will be more important than what they do against the NFC North. After starting the season 0-2 against the division, they don’t have any further margin for error.</p>
